images.caption: Figure 1:Self-Listening is inspired by the human self-monitoring mechanism during speech.Humans hear their own speech through feedback such as bone conduction (left); likewise, self-listening feeds model speech already played to the user back to the LLM (right), grounding the model in what the user has heard.

Figure 2:Anchoring gap in a controlled counting probe.Each system is interrupted while counting from 1 to 30 and is asked to report the last spoken number.
The horizontal axis shows the last number actually spoken (aa), while the vertical axis shows the number subsequently reported by the model (rr).
The dashed diagonal (r=ar=a) represents perfect anchoring.
Vertical segments visualize the anchoring gap,Δanchor=r−a\Delta_{\mathrm{anchor}}=r-a; crosses denote invalid reports.

Figure 3:Overview of the proposed Self-Listening full-duplex model. User speech, model speech, and model text are organized into a three-channel interleaved sequence, while the played waveform is fed back through the self-listening channel to enable anchoring and full-duplex interaction.
